RW01V3.title: GitHub · October 2018 MySQL failover
RW01V3.alert: At 22:52 UTC on October 21, a major developer platform began showing stale metadata after an inter-region connectivity event. Background job processing was disrupted; Git repository data access appeared largely intact. Investigate what failed and the recovery tradeoffs in this reconstruction.
observations: Metadata-related pages showed stale or inconsistent information
Git repository data was still accessible through independent paths
hypotheses: MySQL failover divergence together with deliberate background-job pause
A universal Git repository storage outage
documented_facts: A network partition triggered MySQL Orchestrator leader changes and West Coast failover.
Divergent writes made immediately failing back unsafe.
GitHub paused webhook delivery and Pages builds to prioritize data integrity.
Recovery involved rebuilding replication topologies and restoring replicas.
model_assumptions: 12 illustrative service nodes, dependency edges, initial unavailability inventory and alert proxies
Boolean state of replication topology and protective job pause
Four hypothetical repair choices with synthetic cost units

RW02V3.title: Cloudflare · June 2022 routing outage
RW02V3.alert: At 06:27 UTC on June 21, a global edge network began failing requests in a subset of locations after an infrastructure rollout. Other regions continued to serve traffic. Inspect the reconstructed network to identify the controlling fault.
observations: A subset of high-traffic locations lost external reachability
The outage coincided with an infrastructure change
hypotheses: An attack on all global locations
Incorrect route announcement policy in the affected MCP network
documented_facts: A routing policy configuration change took 19 Cloudflare data centers offline.
The incident affected approximately half of HTTP requests despite 19 centers representing about 4% of locations.
The team rolled back the incorrect route advertisement policy and restored all affected locations by 07:42 UTC.
model_assumptions: Illustrative three-group representation of 19 sites and 10 service nodes
Boolean router policy and capacity flags
Simulated mitigation candidates, costs, and aggregate health outcomes

RW03V3.title: Cloudflare · July 2019 WAF regex outage
RW03V3.alert: At 13:42 UTC on July 2, edge HTTP requests began returning errors around the time of a security-system deployment. Serving-process CPU rose sharply while DNS remained available. Investigate the reconstruction for a cause and safe repair.
observations: An update to a security component was underway
hypotheses: An external DDoS attack saturated bandwidth
WAF regex backtracking exhausted CPU following a rule deployment
Only a CDN cache invalidation problem
documented_facts: A WAF managed-rule deployment contained a pathological regular expression.
Excessive regex backtracking exhausted CPU on HTTP/HTTPS serving processes.
Users received HTTP 502 errors; rollback of the offending rule restored operation.
model_assumptions: 10 simplified modeled components and dependency relationships
Boolean WAF rule and a hypothetical separate safe-guard switch
Simulation-only candidate repair costs and service availability snapshots
